rv.q: The characters, and certainly the acting, have the same type of openhearted vulnerability that made them mean so much to the people who grew up with them.
Despite engaging performances, though, the characters’ motivations don’t always ring true, leading to some frustrating and unconvincing plot developments.

An evening of memory and compelling character study combine in DO SOMETHING PRETTY to tell a finely detailed story that’s filled with all the richness that makes up those unsung moments of everyday life.
A talented ensemble and strong direction by the very talented Jessica Fisch consistently rises to the occasion.
Do Something Pretty speaks to a specific experience that perhaps many cis-women will recognize and it might open others’ eyes to an experience they may not have realized happened around them.

cn.t: Critics find this '80s-set coming-of-age story captures authentic teenage awkwardness through dimensional characters and quiet moments, though the plot itself remains fairly standard. Performances shine in the intimate space.
